_readme: Shared vocabulary for the two labels every job carries: what KIND of work it is
(profession) and what FIELD it is in. Both are facts about the labour market,
true no matter who is looking, which is why they live in sources/ and not in a profile.
Which of these keys belong to a person is the opinion, and that lives in
profiles/<name>/profile.json under `professions` and `fields`.
The two axes are deliberately independent. Project management happens in a hospital and
at YouTube; a profession label on its own cannot tell those apart, which is exactly the
leak this file exists to close. 'Related to me' is profession AND field, never either.
`description` and `examples` are what the profession and field cards show - a sentence on what it is and
real job titles (a profession) or employers (a field) that fall in it - in the wizard and the Profile tab. They classify nothing.
`remote: false` on a profession says the work is mostly done on site; the new-profile
wizard reads it to default the remote question. It filters nothing.
A profession is matched case-insensitively on the title. Only when the title matches nothing is
the description read (its first 1500 characters), and there a keyword counts only right after
'as a', 'als', 'en tant que', 'we are looking for' and the like - elsewhere a body is boilerplate.
Fields are matched on title + description. Keywords have word boundaries, so 'lead' does not fire
on 'leadership' and 'ai' does not fire on 'chain'. A keyword containing a space is matched as a
phrase; a trailing '*' is a stem; a leading '*' matches inside a word, for German compounds
('*berater*' reaches 'Kundenberaterin').
`fields[].categories` maps the employer industries already recorded in
sources/companies.json onto a field, so a posting with a terse title still gets a
field from who is hiring. That only works for jobs pulled from a company connector -
board rows carry a free-text employer name that is not in the registry (65% of Alex's
rows and 84% of Sam's come from a company; the rest depend on the text alone).
Deliberately unmapped: swiss-corporate, scale-up, consulting, remote-first. They say
how big or how remote an employer is, not what field it works in - mapping them would
make On a software company and SIX a bank by assertion rather than by evidence.
The 13 fields cover LinkedIn's 20 top-level industries. Folds (SCHEMA.md "fields"): hospitality, tourism and
wholesale -> retail-consumer; farming and food by what they sell (food for people retail-consumer, feed and
timber industrial); staffing and administrative support -> services; education, government and non-profits
-> academia-public; a holding company -> its operating business's field.
`suggest` on a profession: per skill group, the skills its postings ask for most, which the wizard
offers a person with no CV. Generated by scripts/gen-suggest.ts from an install's market - never hand-edit.

engineering.label: Engineering
engineering.description: Designs, builds and maintains technical systems - software, hardware, machines or infrastructure.

research.label: Research & Development
research.description: Creates new knowledge or products through experiments, studies and scientific work, in a lab, a company R&D team or academia.

clinical.label: Clinical
clinical.description: Runs or supports studies in people - trial design, site management, monitoring and clinical data.

project-management.label: Project & Programme Management
project-management.description: Plans and delivers projects on time and budget - scope, timelines, risks, budgets and the people involved.

product-management.label: Product Management
product-management.description: Decides what a product should be and why - users, market, roadmap - and steers its development.

design.label: Design (UX/UI & Visual)
design.description: Shapes how a product looks and works for the people using it - research, flows, interfaces and visual identity.

management.label: Leadership & Management
management.description: Leads people, teams or whole organisations - direction, budgets, hiring and results.

quality-regulatory.label: Quality & Regulatory
quality-regulatory.description: Makes sure products and processes meet standards and the law - quality systems, audits, approvals and compliance.

data-analytics.label: Data & Analytics
data-analytics.description: Turns data into answers - analysis, statistics, dashboards, data pipelines and models.

manufacturing-operations.label: Manufacturing & Operations
manufacturing-operations.description: Makes and ships things - production, process engineering, supply chain and logistics.

commercial.label: Sales, Marketing & Commercial
commercial.description: Sells and markets products and services - winning customers, campaigns, key accounts and business development.

support-admin.label: Support & Administration
support-admin.description: Keeps an organisation and its customers running day to day - administration, assistance and service desks.

hr.label: People, HR & Recruitment
hr.description: Finds, hires and looks after people - in-house talent acquisition and agency recruitment, HR business partnering, HR operations, pay and benefits, payroll, learning and employee relations.

legal.label: Legal & Compliance
legal.description: Handles law and rules - contracts, advice, disputes, compliance and intellectual property.

finance-accounting.label: Finance & Accounting
finance-accounting.description: Manages money - accounting, controlling, reporting, tax, audit and financial planning.

facilities.label: Facilities & Real Estate
facilities.description: Looks after buildings and workplaces - maintenance, property management and building technology.

education.label: Education & Training
education.description: Teaches and trains - schools, universities, corporate training and course design.

medical.label: Medicine & Pharmacy
medical.description: Diagnoses and treats patients, or advises on medicines - doctors, therapists, practice and pharmacy assistants, pharmacists and medical affairs.

consulting.label: Consulting & Advisory
consulting.description: Advises other organisations as an outside expert - strategy, technology, operations or a specialist field.

retail-sales.label: Retail & Store Sales
retail-sales.description: Sells to the public in shops and stores - serving customers, the till, shelves and running a branch.

care-nursing.label: Nursing & Care
care-nursing.description: Nurses and cares for people - patients, the elderly, children and people who need support - in hospitals, homes, Spitex and childcare.

hospitality.label: Hospitality & Food Service
hospitality.description: Cooks, serves and hosts - restaurants, hotels, canteens, catering and system gastronomy.

skilled-trades.label: Skilled Trades & Crafts
skilled-trades.description: Hands-on craft, building and repair work - mechanics, electricians, carpenters, painters, bakers and butchers, mostly with a vocational certificate.

life-science.label: Life science, pharma & medtech
life-science.description: Pharma, biotech, medical devices and diagnostics - organisations that research, make or test medicines and health technology.

software-it.label: Software & IT
software-it.description: Companies whose product is software, data or IT - tech firms, SaaS, IT services and platforms.

industrial.label: Industrial, engineering & materials
industrial.description: Engineering, machinery, materials and manufacturing - companies that build physical things at scale. Farming and food production go by what they sell: inputs for other businesses (feed, timber, fibres) are industrial, food and drink for people is retail-consumer.

gaming.label: Video games
gaming.description: Studios and publishers that make video games, and the platforms and tools around them.

finance.label: Finance, banking & insurance
finance.description: Banks, insurers, asset managers, payments and fintech.

academia-public.label: Academia & public sector
academia-public.description: Universities, schools, research institutes, government offices, public bodies and non-profits.

health-services.label: Healthcare services
health-services.description: Care for patients - hospitals, clinics, labs and care homes.

retail-consumer.label: Retail, consumer & hospitality
retail-consumer.description: Shops, wholesalers, consumer brands, food and drink, hotels, restaurants and travel - goods and stays sold to the public. Food and drink producers are here; wholesale and hospitality & tourism fold in here too.

services.label: Professional & business services
services.description: Firms that sell expertise or support to other businesses - consulting, audit, legal, staffing, agencies, facility and administrative support.

media-entertainment.label: Media, entertainment & sports
media-entertainment.description: Media, publishing, broadcasting, film and music, the arts, sports clubs and events - organisations that inform or entertain the public. Video games have their own field.

energy-resources.label: Energy, utilities & resources
energy-resources.description: Power, gas and water utilities, oil and gas, mining, and the houses that trade energy and commodities.

transport-logistics.label: Transport & logistics
transport-logistics.description: Moving people and goods - airlines, rail, public transport, shipping, postal, freight forwarding, warehousing and logistics services.

construction-real-estate.label: Construction & real estate
construction-real-estate.description: Building contractors and civil engineering, real estate developers, owners and property managers, and equipment rental.
